versions.changelog:
Version 1.3.2 of continue-learning adds security and privacy controls for learning data.

- Session analysis now requires explicit agent scoping (`--agent <name>` or `--all`); running with no scope is not allowed.
- All session-derived data stored is redacted for secrets and Unicode/control stripped before saving.
- Retention limits added: instincts, evidence, and patterns are capped to recent data; nothing is retained unbounded.
- New `prune` command deletes all stored learning data (instincts, patterns, optimizations).
- Raw transcripts are never persisted; only redacted and aggregated information is stored.
- skill-card.md documentation file removed.

- Renamed the skill from "openclaw-continuous-learning" to "continue-learning".
- Added a new README.md file.
- Removed the skill-card.md file.
- Updated SKILL.md with the new skill name and version.

- Updated documentation to clarify session source directory (`~/.openclaw/agents/`) and improved quick start instructions.
- Enhanced example commands and added a command for showing error patterns.
- Minor version bump and metadata update for improved usability and clearer guidance.

Version 1.2.0

- Added explicit integration guidance for use alongside agent-self-improvement, enabling combined internal (session analysis) and external (user feedback) learning.
- Updated documentation to clarify skill boundaries and workflow for collaborative learning.
- No changes to APIs or storage—improvement is purely in documentation and usability clarity.

openclaw-continuous-learning 1.1.0

- Enhanced description and documentation, detailing instinct-based learning, pattern detection, and confidence scoring.
- Clarified use cases, including agent self-improvement, user preference learning, performance optimization, and error pattern detection.
- Added comprehensive setup and architecture sections with examples and best practices.
- Provided explanation of storage structure and confidence scoring system.
- Included FAQ and related skills for better onboarding and context.
